title: Rust WebRTC sidecar MVP
description: Track the NanoKVM Rust WebRTC sidecar rollout and the evidence needed before it can replace the legacy Go/Pion endpoint by default. The browser contract stays /api/stream/h264; Go remains the authenticated public HTTP/WebSocket boundary; Rust owns WebRTC/media/hardware capture on the rust backend.
design: Test scope is split into host-build, Go boundary, Rust signaling, Rust WebRTC/RTP, hardware capture, packaging/startup, on-device behavior, rollback, and regression suites. Each child issue names the thing under test, the concrete setup, expected observations, and likely failure signals. Keep tests reproducible through nix develop where possible; device-only checks should record exact NanoKVM firmware/library provenance and logs under /data.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every sidecar subsystem has at least one Beads issue with Thing under test, Setup, Assertions, Failure signals, and Evidence to capture.
- Host-side tests cover cargo/go/nix build regressions without NanoKVM hardware.
- Device-side tests cover successful video, reconnect, process isolation from Go/Pion/kvm_system, and rollback.
- Known risky boundaries are explicit: libkvm ABI, hardware prep, H.264 frame shape, ICE/DTLS/SRTP negotiation, and service boot ordering.
notes: Known good manual result: Rust sidecar built from branch ran on NanoKVM at 192.168.1.6 from /data/nanokvm-test/nanokvm-webrtc-rs against /kvmapp/server/dl_lib copied into /data/nanokvm-test/dl_lib, listened on 0.0.0.0:6040, initialized KVM vision, and produced browser video. Do not treat repo-local dl_lib as the known-good runtime set for device validation unless packaging intentionally updates the device libraries.

title: Branch/devshell setup and Rust toolchain additions
description: Validate the NanoKVM flake/devshell and Rust toolchain additions used to build both host checks and RISC-V target artifacts.
design: Thing under test: flake.nix, flake.lock, rust-toolchain.toml, cross target setup, cargo-nextest/rust-analyzer/clang/lld availability, nanokvm-build-webrtc-rs, and nanokvm-build-server. Setup: clean checkout of mjc/rust-webrtc-sidecar on a Nix host with the Sophon host tools path available. Run commands only through nix develop. Assertions: rustc/cargo are pinned, riscv64gc-unknown-linux-musl target builds, Go default server excludes legacy WebRTC/Pion/hardware symbols, legacy server builds with legacy_webrtc tag, generated binaries contain expected rpath to $ORIGIN/dl_lib, and no target/build artifacts are committed. Failure signals: missing target, linker choosing wrong ld, aws-lc/ring target breakage, generated binaries staged, or Go build requiring libkvm for rust backend.
acceptance_criteria:
- nix flake check or equivalent eval succeeds on supported host.
- nix develop -c cargo check --manifest-path server/webrtc-rs/Cargo.toml succeeds.
- nix develop -c cargo test --manifest-path server/webrtc-rs/Cargo.toml succeeds.
- nix develop -c nanokvm-build-webrtc-rs produces server/nanokvm-webrtc-rs for riscv64gc-unknown-linux-musl.
- nix develop -c nanokvm-build-server produces both NanoKVM-Server and NanoKVM-Server-legacy.
- git status after cleaning build outputs contains no generated binaries or target directories.
notes: Capture command output, rustc -Vv, cargo tree -e features for str0m/aws-lc, file server/nanokvm-webrtc-rs, and readelf -d output for rpath/needed libraries where available.

title: Test: H.264 frame handling and RTP emission
description: Test Rust handling of H.264 frames from libkvm through str0m RTP emission.
design: Thing under test: Annex-B frame classification, SPS/PPS/I-frame preservation, P-frame handling, media timestamp increments, playout-delay extension, payload type selection, RTP writer behavior. Setup: host tests with synthetic Annex-B samples and device/browser test with real frames. Assertions: first keyframe includes SPS/PPS before IDR; P-frames are sent after keyframe; MediaTime increments by Screen::frame_duration; negotiated H264 PT is used; frame.data empty never writes RTP; RTCP input does not block transmit. Failure signals: black screen despite positive frame bytes, missing SPS/PPS, wrong PT, nonmonotonic timestamps, repeated first-frame decode failure, or writer missing after connection.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests cover Annex-B NAL detection for SPS/PPS/IDR/P frames.
- Integration log proves negotiated H264 PT and frames_sent increments.
- Browser webrtc-internals shows inbound-rtp bytesReceived and framesDecoded increasing.
- Packet capture or str0m log confirms RTP timestamp progression at configured FPS.
- Empty/error capture result is dropped without RTP write.
notes: Useful evidence: Rust logs around H264 frame read/queued, chrome://webrtc-internals dump, and a short tcpdump/pcap if available.

title: Test: kvmapp libkvm capture ABI and lifecycle
description: Device-only tests for Rust interaction with the known-good kvmapp libkvm.so ABI.
design: Thing under test: dlopen path, kvmv_init, kvmv_hdmi_control, kvmv_read_img, free_kvmv_data, single worker thread lifecycle, error handling. Setup: copy /kvmapp/server/dl_lib to /data/nanokvm-test/dl_lib, deploy Rust binary to /data/nanokvm-test, ensure Go and kvm_system are not running for direct Rust tests. Assertions: KVM vision initializes; capture returns result 3/4 with nonzero bytes; negative results do not crash or free unknown pointers; closing browser stops reads; repeated connect/reconnect does not reinitialize libkvm unsafely. Failure signals: SIGSEGV/SIGABRT, C++ exception, symbol not found, result -1 forever, buffer full -3, leaked capture after disconnect, or dependency on starting Go/kvm_system.
acceptance_criteria:
- Record sha256sum for /kvmapp/server/dl_lib/libkvm.so and libkvm_mmf.so before test.
- Direct Rust process starts and logs KVM vision initialized.
- At least one capture produces result 3 or 4 with nonzero bytes.
- Five connect/disconnect cycles do not crash.
- Process list confirms NanoKVM-Server and kvm_system remain absent during direct Rust test.
notes: Known-good manual hashes are already in nanokvm-y50.3. Any test with repo-local dl_lib should be a separate negative/packaging test, not the default hardware validation.

title: Test: Go rust-backend proxy boundary
description: Test the Go server behavior when built for the Rust backend.
design: Thing under test: /api/stream/h264 route auth boundary, h264_rust.go reverse proxy, build-tag stubs, absence of Pion/hardware init in default Go server. Setup: Go httptest or local server with a fake WebSocket backend on 127.0.0.1:6040; default build only. Assertions: unauthenticated requests are rejected by existing middleware; authenticated upgrade proxies to loopback Rust sidecar; backend unavailable returns 502; default initialize/dispose skip GetKvmVision hardware calls; binary/deps do not include Pion. Failure signals: fallback to legacy WebRTC, proxy before auth, env-controlled target, non-loopback proxy, or default server requiring libkvm.
acceptance_criteria:
- Go test or scripted check covers 502 when sidecar unavailable.
- Go test or route inspection proves middleware.CheckToken remains on /api/stream/h264.
- go list -deps default build contains no github.com/pion/webrtc.
- go list -deps -tags legacy_webrtc contains legacy WebRTC dependency.
- Proxy target is asserted as 127.0.0.1:6040.
notes: Do not change frontend or auth behavior while writing this suite; this is route/proxy/build-tag validation only.

title: Test: boot mode and service process matrix
description: Exercise startup/stop/restart process sets for rust and legacy backend modes.
design: Thing under test: /data/go-app-boot backend selection, S95nanokvm start/stop/restart, packaged binaries, /tmp copy behavior. Setup: device or image test environment with packaged kvmapp/server. Test matrix: no /data/go-app-boot, /data/go-app-boot=rust, /data/go-app-boot=legacy, /data/go-app-boot=pion, and unexpected content. Assertions: rust/default starts nanokvm-webrtc-rs and NanoKVM-Server only; legacy/pion starts kvm_system and NanoKVM-Server-legacy only; stop kills all known processes; restart re-evaluates mode; /tmp/server contains expected binaries. Failure signals: kvm_system in rust mode, NanoKVM-Server-legacy in rust mode, Rust sidecar in legacy mode, stale process after stop, or missing executable bit.
acceptance_criteria:
- Process matrix table is captured in issue comments or docs.
- start/stop/restart each leave expected process set.
- Switching /data/go-app-boot between rust and legacy changes behavior on restart.
- /tmp cleanup uses rm -rf safely and leaves no stale /tmp/server after stop.
- Packaged dl_lib provenance is recorded.
notes: Be careful not to overwrite user device state during test. Use backups for /data/go-app-boot and restore it after validation.

title: Test: browser end-to-end video smoke matrix
description: End-to-end browser tests for Rust WebRTC video with unchanged frontend/browser contract.
design: Thing under test: direct Rust endpoint and packaged Go-proxied endpoint from browser. Setup: NanoKVM with HDMI source, browser on LAN, Rust logs captured. Matrix: Chrome direct ws://DEVICE:6040/api/stream/h264, Firefox direct if available, authenticated app /api/stream/h264 through Go proxy, reload/reconnect, and HDMI source present/absent. Assertions: video appears, framesDecoded increases, reload reconnects, WebSocket stays open, black-screen does not occur when frames are positive, and user-visible frontend remains unchanged. Failure signals: immediate WebSocket close, peer connected but black screen, ICE failed/disconnected, framesDecoded zero, Rust capture result -1 forever, or crash.
acceptance_criteria:
- At least one Chrome direct Rust test shows video and records webrtc-internals.
- At least one packaged Go-proxy test shows video after auth.
- Three reloads reconnect without restarting Rust.
- Browser close stops capture scheduling in logs.
- Failed HDMI/no-signal case is documented with expected UI/log behavior.
notes: Manual baseline exists: user got video on direct Rust after kvmapp lib copy. Convert that into repeatable evidence with logs and browser stats.

title: Test: network and ICE/STUN/TURN configurations
description: Validate network behavior for host candidates, ICE-lite, STUN/TURN config parity, and LAN reachability.
design: Thing under test: NanoKvmConfig ICE conversion, select_bind_ip, UDP bind/candidate advertisement, browser remote candidates, STUN disabled/enabled config. Setup: host unit tests for config conversion and device tests on LAN; optional routed/VPN scenario if NanoKVM deployments require it. Assertions: correct non-loopback IP candidate is advertised; browser host candidates parse; STUN/TURN config from server.yaml maps to frontend iceServers; disabling STUN omits STUN; TURN credentials survive serialization; ICE connects on LAN. Failure signals: candidate advertises 127.0.0.1, mDNS handling closes connection, TURN omitted/malformed, ICE connected only with direct IP but not proxied app, or UDP socket binds wrong interface.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests cover STUN enabled/disabled and TURN config serialization.
- Device logs show UDP socket bound on expected LAN IP.
- Browser selected candidate pair is host/host on LAN smoke test.
- TURN configuration is manually verified or explicitly deferred with reason.
- Candidate parsing handles Chrome and Firefox formats.
notes: Current sidecar uses ICE-lite/host candidate behavior. If internet-routed access is required, create follow-up implementation issue rather than hiding it inside smoke tests.

title: Test: rollback and legacy regression coverage
description: Prove the legacy Go/Pion backend can still be selected and that non-Rust stream paths are not regressed.
design: Thing under test: NanoKVM-Server-legacy, legacy_webrtc build tag, kvm_system startup, MJPEG paths, /api/stream/h264/direct if still supported, and rollback procedure. Setup: packaged device with /data/go-app-boot=legacy or pion; unchanged frontend. Assertions: legacy video path starts; MJPEG path behaves as before; direct H264 path is not broken by build tags; switching back to rust works after rollback test; rollback notes are clear enough for field recovery. Failure signals: no legacy binary, Pion missing in legacy build, kvm_system not started in legacy mode, MJPEG broken, or rollback leaves hardware in bad state.
acceptance_criteria:
- /data/go-app-boot=legacy starts NanoKVM-Server-legacy and kvm_system.
- Legacy /api/stream/h264 works or a blocking issue is filed.
- MJPEG endpoint smoke test passes in legacy mode.
- Direct H264 path behavior is documented.
- Rollback steps include exact file change, restart command, expected process set, and recovery path back to rust.
notes: This is specifically to preserve escape hatches. Do not remove Pion/legacy files until this suite is green and a separate removal issue is approved.

title: Test: stress, soak, and resource cleanup
description: Stress and soak tests for Rust sidecar resource use and cleanup.
design: Thing under test: long-running Rust process, repeated WebSocket/WebRTC sessions, libkvm frame buffers, CPU/memory, file descriptors, UDP sockets, capture scheduling, and hardware state after failures. Setup: device test with HDMI source and script/browser automation. Scenarios: 100 reconnects, 30-minute video soak, browser tab close without close frame, sidecar kill/restart, HDMI cable/source loss and return, network interruption. Assertions: memory and fd count stabilize; no stuck capture when no peers; reconnect succeeds; process restart recovers; device does not require power pull after normal failures. Failure signals: memory growth, fd leak, kvmv buffer full -3, stuck CPU, no video after reconnect, or hardware requiring reboot.
acceptance_criteria:
- 100 reconnect loop completes without Rust crash.
- 30-minute single-session soak keeps video flowing.
- RSS/fd count sampled before/during/after and documented.
- Browser close stops capture scheduling.
- HDMI loss/recovery behavior is observed and either passes or creates a specific bug.
notes: This should run after smoke tests. Save logs under /data/nanokvm-test with timestamps, then summarize in Beads rather than committing logs.

title: Test: observability and failure triage artifacts
description: Define the logs, stats, and artifacts required to diagnose black screen or connection failures quickly.
design: Thing under test: tracing output, frame/candidate counters, browser stats capture, device process checks, kernel crash evidence. Setup: direct Rust and packaged runs. Assertions: logs include sidecar bind address, KVM initialization, ICE state, negotiated H264 payload type, frame read result/bytes/NAL summary, frame queued count, websocket close reason if available, and capture stop. Failure signals: black screen without enough logs to distinguish capture/RTP/browser decode, crash without dmesg capture, or library mismatch not recorded.
acceptance_criteria:
- Document a standard evidence bundle: ps, sha256sum dl_lib, Rust log, dmesg tail, browser webrtc-internals, and exact URL/backend mode.
- Add or verify log lines for the main state transitions.
- Add a script or checklist for collecting evidence from /data without using /tmp.
- Beads issue template for future video bugs includes capture/RTP/browser sections.
notes: This reduces churn during hardware debugging. Keep logs concise enough for normal debug default but complete enough for first-response triage.

title: Rust signaling compatibility
description: Validate that the Rust sidecar remains wire-compatible with the existing frontend signaling protocol.
design: Thing under test: JSON message schema and event flow for ice-servers, video-offer, video-answer, video-candidate, and heartbeat. Setup: run Rust sidecar locally for unit tests and on device for browser tests; use the unchanged frontend or a small WebSocket harness that sends the same message shapes. Assertions: ice-servers is sent first and is JSON encoded like the current frontend expects; offer is accepted; answer serializes as browser-parseable SDP; candidates accept browser JSON candidate wrappers and raw candidate lines; mDNS candidates are ignored safely; heartbeat round trips without disturbing media. Failure signals: browser JSON parse errors, answer rejected by RTCPeerConnection.setRemoteDescription, candidate parse warnings for ordinary host candidates, heartbeat close, or signaling event rename.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests cover Message wire shape and browser candidate parse variants.
- Browser can complete offer/answer without frontend changes.
- Heartbeat response uses event heartbeat and empty data.
- Unknown/empty ICE candidates do not close the WebSocket.
- Regression fixture includes a real frontend offer/candidate sample captured from Chrome or Firefox.
notes: Capture WebSocket transcript with timestamps for one successful connection and one reconnect. Store sanitized samples in tests/fixtures or Beads notes before hardening automated tests.

title: Rust hardware capture via kvmapp libkvm
description: Validate the Rust hardware capture layer that calls the known-good kvmapp libkvm.so ABI from a dedicated worker thread.
design: Thing under test: server/webrtc-rs/src/kvm.rs and its interaction with /kvmapp/server/dl_lib/libkvm.so. Setup: deploy Rust binary under /data/nanokvm-test with dl_lib copied from /kvmapp/server/dl_lib, not repo-local dl_lib unless explicitly testing packaging updates. Start only nanokvm-webrtc-rs. Assertions: libkvm loads from executable sibling dl_lib, kvmv_init runs once, HDMI off/on sequence matches Go boot behavior, all kvmv_read_img/free_kvmv_data calls are serialized on one native worker thread, negative read results do not free/interpret the pointer, positive H.264 reads copy and free exactly once, and the process survives disconnect/reconnect. Failure signals: symbol lookup failure, C++ abort, SIGSEGV in nanokvm-kvm-vision, result -1/-2 loops with zero bytes, buffer-full -3 leaks, or video works only after starting Go/kvm_system.
acceptance_criteria:
- Device smoke test logs KVM vision initialized from Rust.
- /debug/capture or equivalent captures positive result 3 or 4 with nonzero bytes after HDMI is stable.
- First video session sends SPS/PPS/I-frame and subsequent P-frames.
- Reconnect after closing browser does not crash and resumes frame reads.
- Test explicitly records libkvm.so and libkvm_mmf.so sha256 from /kvmapp/server/dl_lib.
notes: Known good device library hashes during manual validation: /kvmapp server libkvm.so 83ac20b143fef11a71855f7982bc592ccbc90a9aa16fba9782c442171fe7883b, libkvm_mmf.so 3dd3f7f3da2f48ce4b52ae57b46c08d50b7187d3b0ecb9dab081ae7a462148c4. Repo-local dl_lib differed and caused failed MMF experiments; that should be tested separately before any library packaging change.

title: RTP/WebRTC media pipeline
description: Validate the Rust WebRTC/RTP media pipeline that replaced Pion for the Rust backend.
design: Thing under test: server/webrtc-rs/src/webrtc_session.rs, str0m configuration, ICE-lite host candidate handling, H.264 codec negotiation, RTP writer, playout-delay extension, media timestamp progression, RTCP drain, and WebSocket lifecycle. Setup: host unit tests for pure parsing/frame helpers; browser/device integration for real SRTP; packet capture if possible on LAN. Assertions: H.264 payload type is negotiated from browser offer; media starts only after RTC connection and video mid/PT are known; frame duration drives monotonic MediaTime; playout-delay extension is registered/written; outgoing UDP continues while RTCP arrives; disconnect stops capture scheduling; reconnect reinitializes media time. Failure signals: black screen with positive frames, ICE connected but frames_sent stays zero, wrong PT, invalid RTP timestamps, missing SPS/PPS on first decoded frame, browser decoder errors, or UDP reader closure.
acceptance_criteria:
- Unit tests cover candidate parsing, Annex-B NAL discovery, and signaling shape.
- Browser stats show inbound video bytes/frames increasing.
- Rust logs show RTCPeer connected, negotiated H264 payload type, H264 frame read result with bytes, and H264 frame queued.
- Reload test shows capture stops and restarts without process restart.
- Chrome and Firefox are each tested or an issue is filed for the missing browser.
notes: Collect chrome://webrtc-internals dump for one successful session and one failed/black-screen session if this regresses. Include selectedCandidatePair, inbound-rtp framesDecoded, bytesReceived, jitter, nackCount, and pliCount.

title: Go authenticated WebSocket proxy
description: Validate that Go remains the authenticated public boundary and proxies /api/stream/h264 to the Rust sidecar without loading legacy WebRTC/Pion or video hardware on the rust backend.
design: Thing under test: build tags, server/backend_rust.go, server/backend_legacy.go, server/common/kvm_vision_stub.go, and server/service/stream/webrtc/h264_rust.go. Setup: build default server and legacy server; inspect imports/symbols; run HTTP tests against a local httptest Rust-WebSocket target if practical. Assertions: default build compiles without legacy_webrtc files, CheckToken middleware remains attached by router, proxy target is fixed 127.0.0.1:6040, sidecar-unavailable returns 502, legacy build retains Pion behavior, and rust backend does not call common.GetKvmVision hardware methods in initialize/dispose. Failure signals: Pion modules in default binary, libkvm needed by default server, unauthenticated h264 path, proxy to non-loopback address from Go, or env-var controlled port/backend state.
acceptance_criteria:
- go list/build default excludes legacy_webrtc files.
- go list/build -tags legacy_webrtc includes legacy WebRTC files.
- Default server has no imports from github.com/pion/webrtc or direct kvm_vision cgo file.
- /api/stream/h264 remains under middleware.CheckToken in router tests or route inspection.
- Rust sidecar unavailable produces Bad Gateway after auth, not fallback to Pion.
notes: Add Go tests around h264_rust.go with a local WebSocket backend and around backend_rust.go/legacy build tags. Keep auth tests focused on route wiring; do not change frontend.

title: Target packaging and service startup
description: Validate target packaging and boot/service startup behavior for rust and legacy backend choices.
design: Thing under test: kvmapp/system/init.d/S95nanokvm, packaged server directory, NanoKVM-Server, NanoKVM-Server-legacy, nanokvm-webrtc-rs, and dl_lib placement. Setup: install built artifacts into kvmapp/server image layout, then test boot-like start/restart/stop commands on device or chroot-equivalent. Assertions: default backend is rust; /data/go-app-boot selects legacy/pion only when its content is legacy or pion; rust path starts nanokvm-webrtc-rs before/with NanoKVM-Server and does not start kvm_system; legacy path starts kvm_system and NanoKVM-Server-legacy; stop/restart kill both possible server binaries and Rust sidecar; dl_lib comes from kvmapp known-good runtime. Failure signals: Go server boots unintentionally during Rust-only device testing, kvm_system starts in rust mode, missing nanokvm-webrtc-rs executable, stale /tmp/server, or wrong dl_lib hashes.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh boot/start with no /data/go-app-boot starts rust sidecar and NanoKVM-Server, not NanoKVM-Server-legacy or kvm_system.
- /data/go-app-boot containing legacy starts NanoKVM-Server-legacy and kvm_system, not Rust sidecar.
- restart changes process set according to current /data/go-app-boot.
- stop removes /tmp/server and /tmp/kvm_system and leaves no matching processes.
- Packaged server directory includes nanokvm-webrtc-rs executable and both Go server binaries.
notes: Record ps output, sha256sum of runtime libs, and S95nanokvm stdout/stderr for each mode. The manual test path used /data/nanokvm-test and intentionally avoided /tmp except stock boot scripts.

title: Hardware validation and rollback notes
description: Validate the hardware MVP on an actual NanoKVM and capture rollback instructions.
design: Thing under test: end-to-end Rust backend on NanoKVM hardware with unchanged frontend. Setup: device on LAN, Go/Pion/kvm_system disabled unless testing packaged boot mode, Rust sidecar listening on 0.0.0.0:6040 for direct testing or loopback behind Go for packaged test. Assertions: browser connects, H.264 video appears, reload/reconnect works, process memory/CPU are stable enough for MVP, HDMI disable/enable state is respected, STUN/TURN config still works when routed through Go config, MJPEG and /api/stream/h264/direct are not regressed in legacy mode. Failure signals: immediate WebSocket close, ICE connected but black screen, KVM vision init failure, result -1 forever, process crash, capture continues after all peers disconnect, or rollback cannot restore legacy video.
acceptance_criteria:
- Successful direct Rust test: ws://DEVICE:6040/api/stream/h264 shows video.
- Successful packaged test: authenticated frontend /api/stream/h264 shows video through Go proxy.
- Three browser reloads reconnect without restarting Rust.
- Closing browser stops frame scheduling within one frame interval plus timeout.
- Rollback to legacy via /data/go-app-boot is documented and manually verified.
- Known-good logs and library hashes are attached in notes or comments.
notes: Manual success already observed: user reported video after Rust sidecar was rebuilt to use kvmapp libkvm.so and /data/nanokvm-test/dl_lib copied from /kvmapp/server/dl_lib. Preserve that as baseline while adding repeatable scripts/tests.

title: Test: host build and dependency hygiene
description: Build a host-side regression suite for the flake, Rust crate, Go build tags, and dependency hygiene.
design: Thing under test: Nix devshell, Rust crate dependency graph, Go default/legacy build separation, generated artifact hygiene. Setup: clean checkout, no device needed. Commands: nix develop -c cargo check/test; nix develop -c cargo nextest run when nextest is available; nix develop -c nanokvm-build-webrtc-rs; nix develop -c nanokvm-build-server; git status check after removing generated outputs. Assertions: default Go server does not import Pion or cgo libkvm path; legacy build does; Rust uses str0m and libloading; Cargo.lock is deterministic; no target/binary artifacts are staged. Failure signals: dirty generated files, unresolved target linker, accidental Pion dependency in default binary, or missing rust target.
acceptance_criteria:
- Script or documented command list runs all host checks through nix develop.
- CI-ready checks fail if server/webrtc-rs/target or server/nanokvm-webrtc-rs is staged.
- Dependency inspection documents Pion absent from default build and present only in legacy_webrtc build.
- RISC-V Rust binary and both Go binaries build from a clean checkout.
notes: Evidence to capture: command transcript, cargo tree, go list -deps for default and legacy builds, and git status after cleanup.

title: Test: Rust signaling protocol compatibility
description: Create automated and captured-browser tests for the Rust sidecar signaling contract.
design: Thing under test: signaling::Message, ice-server conversion, browser candidate parsing, heartbeat, offer/answer flow. Setup: host unit tests plus one browser-generated fixture from unchanged frontend. Assertions: ice-servers payload parses as browser RTCIceServer array; SdpOffer from browser is accepted; SdpAnswer is browser-compatible; candidate wrapper objects and raw candidate strings are accepted; end-of-candidates and mDNS candidates are ignored without closing. Failure signals: event mismatch, JSON escaping mismatch, rejected answer, WebSocket close on candidate, or heartbeat starvation.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fixtures include at least one real video-offer and video-candidate from the NanoKVM frontend.
- Unit tests cover ice-servers, heartbeat, candidate JSON, candidate raw string, empty candidate, and mDNS candidate.
- Browser harness can connect to Rust sidecar and reach video-answer without media capture enabled.
- Test output records exact event sequence.
notes: Keep frontend unchanged. Sanitized fixture data can live under server/webrtc-rs/tests/fixtures if added later.
